questions.q: What structurally distinguishes a Matrix from a Table?
options: A Matrix groups data both by rows and by columns, producing a genuine cross-tabulation; a Table only groups by rows
A Matrix cannot contain any numeric data
A Matrix is just a Table renamed — there's no functional difference
A Matrix can only be built in SSDT, never in Report Builder
questions.explain: A Table groups data down the page (rows only). A Matrix groups both ways — rows and columns — the same shape as a pivot table.

questions.q: In the Table or Matrix Wizard, what does dragging a field into Column groups do that a Table doesn't use?
options: It creates a horizontal grouping dimension, so the field's distinct values become columns across the report
It has no effect unless Row groups is left empty
It deletes the Row groups selections
Column groups only affect font formatting
questions.explain: Column groups is the box that makes a matrix a matrix — it adds the horizontal grouping dimension that a plain Table never uses.

questions.q: Why is Microsoft's own documentation blunt about matrices getting "quickly wide"?
options: Because every new distinct value in a column-group field adds another column, which can be a real problem for printed pages or PDF exports
Because matrices always render at a fixed width regardless of data
Because column groups are limited to exactly two values
Because matrices cannot be exported at all
questions.explain: Unlike a Table (which only grows taller), a Matrix can grow wider as well — expanding a subcategory with many distinct values can make the report expand horizontally across many pages when printed.

questions.q: What's one practical fix for a matrix that's expanding too far horizontally for a printed page?
options: Rotate a text box 270 degrees using the WritingMode property so labels run vertically instead of consuming horizontal space
Delete the Column groups entirely, which also deletes the data
Matrices cannot be resized in any way
Switch the report's page orientation setting, which is the only fix available
questions.explain: Setting WritingMode to Rotate270 on a text box (like a territory-name column) lets labels run vertically, saving horizontal space alongside resizing columns down to only what's needed.

questions.q: After finishing the Table or Matrix Wizard for a matrix with Territory in Row groups and Subcategory in Column groups, where do you confirm both grouping hierarchies were created correctly?
options: Both the Row Groups pane and the Column Groups pane at the bottom of the design surface
Only in the Report Data pane's Parameters folder
Matrices don't have a Grouping pane at all
Only by exporting the report to PDF first
questions.explain: A matrix populates both the Row Groups pane and the Column Groups pane — seeing both filled in confirms it has two independent grouping hierarchies, not one.
